newsitem.title: FRANCE: France hails Israeli halt of Jerusalem plan.
newsitem.headline: France hails Israeli halt of Jerusalem plan.

text.p: France on Tuesday hailed Israel's decision to block construction of a new Jewish quarter in Arab East Jerusalem and expressed hopes for similar moves to defuse other flashpoints.
"We approve the Israeli government's decision and hope similar moves to defuse the situation will be taken in other places," foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said.
He was commenting on the Israeli Interior Ministry's suspension of a permit to build 70 Jewish homes in the Ras al-Amoud Arab neighbourhood on the edge of East Jerusalem.

Doutriaux's reference to defusing the situation "in other places" apparently referred to Israeli building at Har Homa, a desert area south of the city but within its official boundaries and known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim.
Relations between Israel and the Palestinians have been in crisis since March, when Israel broke ground for the project.
Doutriaux said Paris "disapproves of building (new) settlements, especially in Jerusalem where we hope the status quo will be maintained pending Israeli-Palestinian negotiations on the issue".

"The most important thing now is to work for the restoration of confidence and take all the necessary decisions to relaunch the application of peace accords. We will back these efforts," he told reporters.

Israel, which annexed East Jerusalem after capturing it in 1967, says it can build where it likes in the city it calls its united capital. Palestinians say East Jerusalem will be the capital of their future state.
